A.title: OPTION A  ·  HARBOUR CITY
A.name: MERIDIAN
A.subtitle: A walled free port of the Triple Alliance. Nine quarters round a central harbour; every lane is busy.
A.concept: Meridian is the Triple Alliance's free port, the richest city on the lanes. It is built like a harbour town: a walled ring 4.6 km across, a docking spire at its heart, and nine quarters between the boulevard and the wall, each run by the people who work there. You arrive from deep space in the inbound stream, behind a liner, with the skyline filling the screen. You pass under the gatehouse towers and the customs scan, and Harbour Control hails you. Everything you can do in the game happens somewhere in the city, for a reason.
strengths: The most city-like: you are surrounded by buildings and traffic everywhere you fly
Every quarter is one flight from the harbour along its avenue: easy to learn, easy to return
Hazards sit where a city would have them: the reactor, the defences, the quarry
costs: The ring layout repeats; districts need strong silhouettes to tell apart
callouts: You spawn here, in the inbound stream, with the city ahead
Harbour Mouth: customs scan, signals, MERIDIAN overhead

B.title: OPTION B  ·  THE KEEL
B.name: THE KEEL
B.subtitle: A city grown along the 5.4 km keel of the colony ship that brought people here.
B.concept: The colony ship that brought the first settlers never left. Its 5.4 km keel became a street, its ribs became the city's blocks, and three centuries of building filled the bays between them. Traffic runs up the east flank and down the west, and through the keel's own arches. You arrive at the bow and look up the whole length of the city, its lights running away into the distance. The ship's reactor still pulses and its stern engines still fire.
strengths: The grandest arrival: the whole city in one long perspective
A single spine is impossible to get lost on
The ship's own history explains the reactor and the engine wash
costs: Linear: the far end is 5 km from the bow
Districts on a flank feel like bays, less like quarters of a city

C.title: OPTION C  ·  THE CROWN
C.name: THE CROWN
C.subtitle: Station islands round an Aksharan gate, 1.3 km high, that still works.
C.concept: Nobody built the Crown. It is an Aksharan gate, a hoop 1.3 km across standing through the plane, and it still opens onto other systems. A city of station islands grew around it to tax what comes through. Ships arrive in a flash between its feet every few seconds. The Vestari say it is holy and keep a sanctum at its foot; everyone else just trades.
strengths: The strongest landmark in the game: a 1.3 km gate rising toward the camera
Arrivals are a show: ships flash in through the gate all the time
costs: Islands with open space between them: less like a city, more like an archipelago
The gate's lore commits the mystery (the Aksharans) early

D.title: OPTION D  ·  MERIDIAN ON THE HOLE
D.name: MERIDIAN
D.subtitle: Option A rebuilt round a black hole: the city's power, its ring road and its first lesson.
D.concept: Meridian was built on a black hole for its power: eight Siphons, 450 m arms, reach in to the disk's edge, pull plasma off it with magnetic nozzles and drive it into converters that feed every quarter.  The hole's pull is the city's first lesson: you feel it from the outer markers, the inbound lane bends into the Current, the 1300 m orbit that is the city's ring road (cut your engines and you circle for free), and red buoys mark the Horizon Line past which a starter ship cannot climb out. The Breakers feed scrap down the Drain; every wreck makes the disk flare, and the converters' lee is the shelter. Nothing here stands on a floor: rings spin for weight, drums point at the hole, radiators stand edge-on to it, and the city carries on in lower orbits beneath you.
strengths: One idea explains the whole city: power, traffic, hazards and layout all come from the hole
Teaches the gravity well by living with it: the pull, orbits, the Horizon Line, slingshots
Megastructures: each quarter is a few huge connected slabs threaded by flight streets
costs: Gravity everywhere: AI traffic must fly against it (it already uses real thrusters)
A black hole needs a new look: lensing, the disk and flares are new VFX
callouts: You spawn outside, in the inbound stream; you feel the pull from here
Harbour Mouth: gun keeps, batteries, the picket, mine belts, customs

E.title: OPTION E  ·  THE HOLLOW
E.name: THE HOLLOW
E.subtitle: A pirate haven built into an asteroid: tunnels and caverns inside, construction built onto the rock.
E.concept: The Khuchad Clan's haven, built into a two-lobed asteroid 1.7 km long. You come in through the rock field along a few beacons to the Maw. Inside, the Ring highway runs round both lobes at the flight plane, two ways, lit by working lamps. Off it are the Market (the black market, in the largest cavern), four merchants' dens, the pirates' Docks and the Den, a warship rammed into the rock. Outside, the station is built onto the rock: docking spars, modules bolted to the cliffs, scaffolding, a girder belt round its waist and an ore mass driver. Inside the rock the roof hides round you, so the tunnels fly like streets.
strengths: Small and quiet: about forty ships, every one with a reason to be there
Tunnels and caverns are a new kind of flying: tight, two-way, lit
A different feel from Meridian: rough, hidden, one clan's rock
costs: Tunnels need the roof cutaway round the player (the camera looks down)
Defended for the coming alien attack: about 30 guns to run as AI turrets, most at the Maw
The rock is voxels at 12 m: about 8,000 columns to build and to collide with
